Team — did a quick back-of-envelope and ran the Nebula profile through our cost sim (attached: redwood_cost_sim_v2.xlsx). Key findings / recommendation:

Summary recommendation (pilot): hybrid mix — prioritize memory-heavy H100s for long-context research nodes, A100s for medium-context chat/finetune workloads, and L4s for high-concurrency embedding / low-cost chat.
Pilot sizing (12-week validation):
- H100 (80GB) x 6 nodes: dedicated for long-context retrieval / research. Rationale: KV cache + sharded models for 10k+ sequences; H100 memory avoids frequent spilling and keeps tail latencies acceptable. Estimated p95 token latency for long-context pipeline: ~420ms.
- A100 (40GB) x 12 nodes: general-purpose chat model serving and few-shot finetuning. Good balance for throughput vs memory. Expected sustained throughput ~70k tokens/sec aggregate with modest batching.
- L4 (48GB) x 40 nodes: embeddings and high-concurrency stateless chat. Best $/token for short-context inference; useful for bulk embedding jobs.

Memory / perf tradeoffs:
- Long-context (10k+): requires significant KV cache memory. With H100 we avoid model-partitioning overhead; A100 will work but will see +15-25% tail latency and occasional OOMs under worst-case prefixes.
- Throughput: L4s outperform on cost-per-embedding and low-latency short requests due to optimized int8 paths; they are not suitable for very long contexts or large dense KV caches.
- Fallthrough strategy: route conversational queries to A100 pool and long-context retrieval to H100. If H100 capacity exhausted, queue/espouse shorter context fallbacks to A100 with graceful decline in response length and a note to app to re-query.

Cost and commercial notes (ballpark, pilot rate card applied):
- Pilot monthly consumption estimate: ~$85k–$110k (mix dependent on utilization — sim shows 35% utilization steady-state for pilot workloads).
- Unit economics: H100 ~2.6x A100 on $/hour but gives 3.8x memory density; L4 is ~0.3x A100 $/hour for embedding workloads. See attached workbook for per-token breakdown.

Operational considerations:
- Autoscale warm pools for H100-backed endpoints (spin-up cold-starts cost time; pre-warm keys for heavy experiments).
- KV caching policy: dedicate 60% of H100 memory to KV cache for retrieval pipelines; persist cold segments to shared SSD layer (adds ~70ms on cache-miss).
- Rollout: start with 50% traffic to pilot fleet, run synthetic regression tests (latency, token quality) and then scale to 100% for customers in the pilot cohort.

Next steps: I can flesh this into a 1-pager for Procurement + a technical appendix (SLOs, failover policy) by EOD. Questions?

—Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
